key.description: Where agent definitions can live and the priority ordering when definitions exist at multiple levels. Common scopes: project, user/personal, managed/enterprise, CLI-defined.
What format agent definitions use. Varies widely: Markdown with YAML frontmatter, JSON config files, TOML sections, or AGENTS.md plain markdown.

definition_format.mechanism: Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (same frontmatter as skills) followed by the system prompt, as agents/<name>.md or agents/<name>/AGENT.md

automatic_delegation.mechanism: the agent sees each profile's description and chooses the most appropriate one when spawning a subagent

background.mechanism: subagents run in the foreground or background and can be switched while running

natural_language.mechanism: the user can ask the agent to use a specific profile by name

key.description: How agents are triggered. Mechanisms include natural language detection, @-mention syntax, slash commands, CLI flags, or automatic delegation.
Whether per-agent model overrides are supported, allowing different agents to use different AI models.

model_selection.mechanism: model frontmatter field overrides the subagent's model (default is the router-selected subagent model, not the parent's)

key.description: Whether agents can spawn, delegate to, or resume other agents. Enables multi-agent coordination patterns.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-AGENT §9.1 (DERIVABLE; canonical spawn tool name, ACIF-CORE Appendix A)

subagent_spawning.mechanism: max-nesting frontmatter field lets a custom subagent spawn its own subagents; nesting is disabled by default

key.description: Whether agents can be restricted to specific tools via allowlists, denylists, tool categories, or per-tool configuration maps.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-AGENT §9.1 (DERIVABLE); tool vocabulary ACIF-CORE Appendix A

tool_restrictions.mechanism: allowed-tools frontmatter list (alias tools) restricts which tools the subagent can use

key.description: Whether hooks can inject messages, system prompts, or conversation context into the agent's active session.

context_injection.mechanism: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext injects text into the agent's context (UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart examples)

key.description: Which decision actions hooks can take on the triggering action. Contents: {block: bool, allow: bool, modify: bool}. Mechanisms include exit code contracts, JSON decision fields, or cancel flags. Boundary: decision_control governs whether a tool invocation proceeds; see permission_control for whether a tool is available at all.

decision_control.mechanism: top-level decision "approve" or "block" with optional reason; exit code 2 blocks (documented under 'Output format' / 'Exit Codes')

key.description: What kinds of executors hooks support beyond shell commands. May include HTTP endpoints, LLM prompt evaluation, multi-turn agent handlers, or TypeScript extensions.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-HOOK §10.1 (DERIVABLE); handler-type enum ACIF-HOOK Appendix B, §8.2

handler_types.mechanism: each hook has a type of "command" (shell command) or "prompt" (LLM prompt evaluation), documented under 'Hook Format'

key.description: Where hooks can be configured and the precedence model when multiple scopes define hooks for the same event. Common scopes: global/user, project, workspace, managed/enterprise.

hook_scopes.mechanism: project (.devin/hooks.v1.json, .devin/config.json, .devin/config.local.json) and user (~/.config/devin/config.json) scopes documented under 'Project-Level' / 'User-Level (Global)'

key.description: Whether hooks can modify tool input arguments before the tool executes. Safety-critical capability — silent degradation creates false security. Minimum qualification: supported when the provider provides any mechanism to modify tool input arguments before execution (e.g., hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput, plugin-mutable args, or equivalent).

input_modification.mechanism: PreToolUse hooks rewrite tool input via hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput, merged into the tool's arguments before execution

key.description: Whether hooks communicate with the host via structured JSON on stdin/stdout rather than plain text or exit codes alone.

json_io_protocol.mechanism: event data passed as JSON on stdin; JSON output on stdout, documented under 'Command Hooks'

key.description: Whether hooks can filter which tools or events they respond to using name matching, regex patterns, or structured criteria.

matcher_patterns.mechanism: matcher is a regex against the event's tool_name; empty or omitted matches all tools (documented under 'Using the Matcher' / 'Tool names you can match')

key.description: Whether hooks can make or influence permission decisions determining whether a tool is available for invocation. Minimum qualification: supported when the provider allows hooks to return permission decisions of any kind (grant, deny, or ask). Boundary: permission_control governs whether a tool is available; see decision_control for invocation-flow control.

permission_control.mechanism: PermissionRequest event fires when a permission decision is needed and can approve or block it

key.description: Whether the provider supports organization-level MCP configuration management, including managed server lists, allowlists, and enterprise registries.

enterprise_management.mechanism: organization-level MCP admin controls (allowlist, custom registries, regex matching) documented under 'Admin Controls (Teams & Enterprises)' / 'Admin Configuration Guidelines' headings

key.description: Whether MCP server configuration supports environment variable expansion. Reduces the need for hardcoded secrets in config files.

env_var_expansion.mechanism: ${env:VAR_NAME} and ${file:/path} interpolation documented under 'Config Interpolation' heading

key.description: Whether the provider offers an in-IDE MCP server discovery and installation experience.

marketplace.mechanism: in-IDE MCP marketplace documented under 'MCP Registry' / 'Configuring Custom Registries' headings

key.description: Which per-server tool filtering mechanisms the provider supports. Contents: {allowlist: bool, blocklist: bool, disable_flag: bool}. Controls which server tools are exposed to the agent. Boundary: tool_filtering governs tool visibility (what appears in the agent's available tool set); see auto_approve for execution gating of visible tools.

tool_filtering.mechanism: per-server tool filtering documented under 'Configuring MCP tools' (per-server disabledTools array in mcp_config.json, 100-tool cap; the UI toggle is per server) and 'MCP Allowlist' (admin-side regex matching) headings

key.description: Which MCP transport protocols the provider supports. Common transports: stdio (local process), SSE (Server-Sent Events), HTTP/streamable-HTTP (stateless or streaming).

transport_types.mechanism: transport types (stdio for local, Streamable HTTP and SSE for remote) documented under 'Remote HTTP MCPs' heading; remote servers use serverUrl/url instead of command/args

always.mechanism: always_on trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — full rule content included in system prompt every message

glob.mechanism: glob trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — activated when files matching glob pattern are in context

manual.mechanism: manual trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — activated via @-mention

model_decision.mechanism: model_decision trigger value documented in 'Activation Modes' table — Cascade decides based on context

key.description: How rules decide when to load into context. Providers implement varying modes: always-on, conditional/glob-based, model-decision, and manual activation. Tracks which modes the provider supports and how they are configured.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-RULE §9.1 (DERIVABLE); activation-mode vocabulary ACIF-RULE Appendix A, §10

key.description: Whether the provider auto-generates persistent rules from conversation context. Distinct from user-authored rules — these are AI-created and stored separately.

auto_memory.mechanism: Cascade-managed Memories layer auto-writes context based on conversation (documented under 'Memories & Rules' / 'How to Manage Memories')

agents_md.mechanism: AGENTS.md fallback documented in dedicated rules.1 doc with 'Comparison with Rules' section

key.description: Which rule file formats from other providers this provider recognizes. Contents: recognized_formats (list of filenames like AGENTS.md, .cursorrules, .windsurfrules). Minimum qualification: supported when the provider reads at least one rule-file format defined by a different provider.
Whether rules load from multiple directory levels with defined precedence. Enables project-root rules plus subdirectory-scoped overrides.

hierarchical_loading.mechanism: .devin/rules/ (preferred; .windsurf/rules/ legacy fallback) scanned in current workspace, sub-directories, and parent dirs up to git root (documented under 'Rules Discovery' / 'Rules Storage Locations')

key.description: Whether the provider supports automatic model-driven skill invocation — the model selects and activates a skill without explicit user syntax. Implementations vary: description-field semantic matching, explicit keyword arrays, and boolean flags are all equivalent mechanisms for the same concept. Note: a description field paired with an opt-out disable_model_invocation flag is functionally equivalent to an explicit auto_invocable boolean — both express that the skill participates in automatic activation unless suppressed.
key.spec_ref: ACIF-SKILL §10.1 (DERIVABLE); activation enum ACIF-SKILL §6.2, Appendix A

auto_invocable.mechanism: Cascade invokes a skill when the request matches its description (documented under 'Automatic Invocation')

key.description: The required or conventional filename for this skill type. For example, "SKILL.md" for Claude Code skills.

canonical_filename.mechanism: SKILL.md is the fixed filename in each skill directory (documented under 'SKILL.md File Format')

key.description: What the skill does. Used by the AI to decide when to auto-invoke it. Also shown in skill listings and help text.

description.mechanism: description frontmatter field used for automatic invocation (documented under 'Required Frontmatter Fields')

key.description: Human-readable display name for the skill. If omitted, the directory name is used. Shown in skill listings and menus.

display_name.mechanism: name frontmatter field (documented under 'Required Frontmatter Fields')

key.description: Whether the skill can be installed at global/personal scope (applies across all projects for the current user).
Whether the skill can be installed at project scope (applies to current project only, typically committed to version control).
Whether the skill can be installed at shared/enterprise scope (applies to all users in an organization or shared environment).

shared_scope.mechanism: OS-level system skills deployed by enterprise IT (documented under 'System-Level Skills (Enterprise)')

key.description: Whether the skill directory may contain arbitrary co-located files (scripts, templates, configs, checklists) beyond SKILL.md that the agent can access when the skill is invoked. Enables multi-file skill bundles without converting supporting files into separate skills or rules.

skill_bundled_resources.mechanism: supporting files alongside SKILL.md in the skill directory (documented under 'Adding Supporting Resources')

key.description: When false, the skill is hidden from user-facing menus (e.g., the / command menu). The AI can still invoke it. Default: true.

user_invocable.mechanism: @-mention a skill by name (documented under 'Manual Invocation')
